question: Can a VAE's latent width be selected cheaply by training several short-run models and binary-searching for the largest width at which intrinsic-dimension estimates of posterior means and posterior samples have not yet separated?

key_findings.claim: The released scores support the paper's basic descriptive observation: posterior-sample intrinsic dimension rises toward the nominal bottleneck width after passive coordinates appear, while posterior-mean intrinsic dimension saturates much earlier.
key_findings.evidence: Across the three plotted convolutional VAE sweeps, the sampled curve separates sharply from the mean curve as width grows, and the variable-type plots associate this region with increasing mixed and passive coordinates. The archived 53,685 score rows independently reproduce the reported data MLE(k=20) averages of about 4.05 for Symsol, 11.49 for dSprites, and 22.12 for CelebA, while TwoNN gives about 3.52, 11.05, and 29.36. The signal is a useful early-training diagnostic of stochastic unused capacity, not by itself a definition of an optimal representation.

key_findings.claim: FONDUE is substantially cheaper than the paper's full-width training sweep in the three reported settings, but the experiment measures a proxy-search cost rather than validating optimal model selection.
key_findings.evidence: For convolutional VAEs, Table 1 reports 11.0±0.0 dimensions in 7 minutes on Symsol, 12.2±0.4 in 20 minutes on dSprites, and 50.2±0.9 in 14 minutes on CelebA, using five to nine short model trainings of one or two epochs. A fully trained model is said to take about two hours on the same A100 GPUs. The comparison does not report an end-to-end grid-search wall time, energy, carbon, validation likelihood, FID, downstream utility, or retrained selected-model quality, so it establishes speed for locating the chosen threshold crossing, not that the crossing is an optimal width.

key_findings.claim: The term 'optimal dimensionality' is not operationally or statistically justified by the paper's evaluation.
key_findings.evidence: The algorithm defines its answer as the last width before one hand-set IDE-gap threshold is crossed, then judges that answer by visual agreement with flattening training reconstruction and regularization curves generated by the same model family. There is no ground-truth optimal width, held-out model-selection objective, downstream task, sample-quality metric, likelihood comparison, or comparison with other automatic-selection methods. The convolutional selections also exceed the known factor counts substantially: 11 versus two factors for Symsol and 12.2 versus five for dSprites. This can still be a defensible capacity heuristic, but 'optimal' is circular under the evidence supplied.

key_findings.claim: The printed threshold specification contains a hundred-fold inconsistency; the released contemporaneous configuration resolves the intended experiment but not the paper as written.
key_findings.evidence: The prose states t=0.2 and calls it 20% of the data IDE, while Algorithm 1 computes threshold=t×p/100. With t=0.2 this is 0.2%, not 20%. The repository revision immediately preceding submission instead sets threshold=20 and computes threshold=(cfg.threshold×pivot)/100, which yields the intended 20%. The current repository later changed the implementation to an absolute cfg.threshold with default 1. Thus a literal implementation of the PDF differs by 100×, and a current-code run differs semantically from the 2022 experiment unless pinned to the historical revision.

key_findings.claim: The MLE estimator described in the equations is not the estimator used by the released implementation, contradicting the paper's explanation of its CelebA result.
key_findings.evidence: Equations 4-5 define per-point estimates using 1/(k-1) and then average their reciprocals, which the text identifies as the original Levina-Bickel averaging. The paper explicitly says Pope et al. used the MacKay-Ghahramani alternative. In both the submission-era and current code, however, _compute_mle sums the neighbor log ratios, divides by k-2, averages those log statistics across points, and only then takes one reciprocal: the bias-corrected global-inverse form associated with the MacKay correction. The constructor stores a seed but the estimator ignores it and calls global np.random.shuffle. Consequently the method identity, claimed source of the 22-versus-26 CelebA discrepancy, and exact repeatability are all misreported.

key_findings.claim: The correctness theorem proves only a conditional binary-search property after assuming the central monotonic behavior, and even its termination claim needs an unstated upper crossing.
key_findings.evidence: Axiom 1 assumes that every width below threshold is smaller than every width above threshold; that is exactly the single-crossing structure required by the doubling/binary search. Under a nonempty upper set and deterministic evaluations, the returned boundary result is routine. But the axiom is based only on the observed datasets, noisy short-run estimates are not proved monotone, and if no tested width ever exceeds the threshold, u remains infinite and p doubles forever. The theorem says 'any execution' returns without assuming B is nonempty or imposing a maximum width. It therefore establishes neither estimator validity nor unconditional termination.

key_findings.claim: Posterior collapse is a documented confound that the algorithm itself does not test for.
key_findings.evidence: The paper correctly shows that both benign selective passivity and pathological posterior collapse create a large sample-versus-mean IDE gap. It says the cases are distinguishable because full collapse has high reconstruction loss and few active variables. Yet FONDUE's decision rule observes only IDE_z−IDE_mu; neither Algorithm 1 nor GET-MEM checks reconstruction, KL balance, active-coordinate count, or model quality. A poorly trained short-run model can therefore trigger the same stopping condition the method interprets as excess capacity.

key_findings.claim: The architecture and autoencoder generalization claims are much broader than the experiments.
key_findings.evidence: Architecture robustness is tested only by repeating the three datasets with one fully connected family; its chosen widths shift materially relative to the convolutional family (8 versus 11 on Symsol, 6.6 versus 12.2 on dSprites, and 39 versus 50.2 on CelebA). Deterministic autoencoders cannot run the mean-versus-sample rule at all; the paper only plots reconstruction for AEs with an equivalent architecture and suggests reusing the VAE-selected width. No differing decoder family, likelihood, prior, beta, resolution, modality, or modern hierarchical VAE is tested, and no AE baseline verifies that the transferred width is best.

key_findings.claim: The public score archive is valuable and hash-verifiable, but its CelebA sweep is not the balanced five-seed grid described in the paper.
key_findings.evidence: The official Kent archive has the advertised MD5 and contains 53,685 score rows for five estimators, three datasets, convolutional/final, checkpoint, fully connected, and beta=20 runs. However, in the main CelebA beta=1 file, seed 0 has widths 3,6,8,10,12,18,24,32,100,150,200 but lacks 42,52,62; seeds 1-4 contain 42,52,62 but lack width 18. Thus width 18 is represented by one model seed and widths 42,52,62 by four, contrary to the stated five repetitions at all base widths plus the extra CelebA widths. Any plotted band or cross-width comparison at those locations has unequal replication.

key_findings.claim: The released repository enables inspection but does not provide a pinned, turnkey reproduction of the paper's central tables.
key_findings.evidence: The public repository contains the FONDUE implementation, model/data code, Hydra configurations, and plotting utilities, and the official data deposit provides score TSVs. But there is no paper release or tag, lockfile, container, test suite, raw FONDUE run log, selected-model checkpoint, or current pretrained-model link. The reproduction page retains unresolved model_url and ide_url placeholders and commands such as compute_ide and visualise_ides.sh that are absent from the current command set. The submission-era FONDUE entry point did not set TensorFlow or NumPy seeds; cfg.seed affected the sampler, while MLE ignored its own seed. Current HEAD f6d6e66 (2023-09-04) also changes the threshold semantics and lower bound relative to the PDF. The experiment is partially reproducible with historical reconstruction work, not replayable verbatim from one pinned artifact.

key_findings.claim: Several rendered implementation details are internally inconsistent, which matters because exact architectural replay is part of the robustness claim.
key_findings.evidence: The main text says every image is resized to 64×64, but Tables 3-4 print encoder inputs as R^(64×63×channels). Both architecture tables hard-code a ten-dimensional bottleneck (2×10 encoder output and R^10 decoder input) despite the experiment varying widths from 3 to 200. These are likely transcription/example errors rather than the executed shapes, but the tables do not label them as such. Exact replay therefore requires consulting code rather than following the paper alone.

method.core_idea: Use the emergence of a gap between the intrinsic dimensions of posterior samples and posterior means as an early signal that a VAE bottleneck has begun allocating coordinates to passive prior-like noise.
method.mechanism: Estimate the input-data intrinsic dimension, use it as an initial integer pivot, train a fresh VAE for a small number of epochs at that width, and compute MLE intrinsic dimensions for the encoder mean and sampled representations. If the sampled-minus-mean gap is at most a fixed fraction of the initial estimate, double the pivot; once the gap exceeds the threshold, binary-search between the last passing and first failing widths. Memoize evaluated widths and return the last passing integer. Repeat with more epochs until the selected width appears stable.
assumptions: The VAE reaches a benign polarized regime within one or a few epochs rather than transient or global posterior collapse.
Passive coordinates cause a reliably positive sampled-minus-mean IDE gap, while all useful active or mixed coordinates stay below the chosen threshold.
The pass/fail classification is monotone in bottleneck width despite stochastic initialization, minibatches, posterior sampling, and IDE estimation.
There exists a finite width that fails the threshold so the doubling phase terminates.
A 20% data-IDE threshold transfers across datasets, architectures, training durations, and estimator bias without tuning.
MLE with Euclidean neighborhoods on 10,000 high-dimensional activations gives a stable enough global dimension estimate for binary decisions.
Avoiding passive variables provides the desired reconstruction-regularization tradeoff and is an adequate surrogate for application-specific model quality.
Several independently initialized short-run models are cheaper and sufficiently predictive of fully trained candidate models.
A VAE-derived choice transfers to a deterministic autoencoder only when dataset and architecture are effectively identical.
Integer truncation of the data IDE and the exact estimator-averaging convention do not materially alter the search path.

techniques.role: Measures local-neighborhood intrinsic dimension with MLE and uses TwoNN as a diagnostic comparison.
Contrasts mean and sampled posterior representations to detect prior-like passive coordinates.
Doubles bottleneck width until a threshold crossing, then binary-searches the boundary.
Caches IDE pairs so a candidate width is not retrained within one search.
Repeats searches with increasing short training durations until the selected width stops moving.
Classifies active, mixed, and passive coordinates to interpret the observed IDE divergence.
Uses beta=20 on dSprites to illustrate that pathological collapse also inflates sampled IDE.
Repeats the heuristic on convolutional and fully connected VAE families.

evaluations.setting: Convolutional beta=1 VAE on reduced Symsol; five reported runs; minimum stable search duration two epochs
evaluations.metric: Selected bottleneck width and wall time
evaluations.result: 11.0±0.0 dimensions in 7 minutes; six models trained
evaluations.baseline: A fully trained model is reported to take about two hours on the same NVIDIA A100 GPUs; no competing selector is evaluated

evaluations.setting: Convolutional beta=1 VAE on dSprites; five reported runs; one search epoch
evaluations.metric: Selected bottleneck width and wall time
evaluations.result: 12.2±0.4 dimensions in 20 minutes; five models trained
evaluations.baseline: True dataset factor count is five and archived MLE(k=20) data IDE averages about 11.49; no held-out optimum is supplied

evaluations.setting: Convolutional beta=1 VAE on CelebA; five reported runs; one search epoch
evaluations.metric: Selected bottleneck width and wall time
evaluations.result: 50.2±0.9 dimensions in 14 minutes; nine models trained
evaluations.baseline: Archived MLE(k=20) data IDE averages about 22.12 and prior work reported 26; reconstruction continues to improve beyond the selected width

evaluations.setting: Fully connected beta=1 VAEs on Symsol, dSprites, and CelebA
evaluations.result: 8.0±0.0, 6.6±0.5, and 39.0±0.6 dimensions, requiring 6, 1, and 9 epochs respectively
evaluations.baseline: Convolutional selections are 11.0, 12.2, and 50.2, showing architecture dependence rather than a dataset-only optimum

evaluations.setting: Convolutional deterministic autoencoders on the same three datasets
evaluations.result: Plots are reported as performing well near VAE-selected widths
evaluations.baseline: No automatic AE selector, uncertainty, validation metric, or numerical best-width comparison is reported

evaluations.setting: beta=20 convolutional VAE on dSprites with ten latent coordinates
evaluations.metric: Layerwise IDE profile under induced posterior collapse
evaluations.result: Mean and late-layer IDEs collapse while sampled IDE is inflated toward nominal width
evaluations.baseline: The same mean-sample divergence drives FONDUE, but its decision rule does not inspect reconstruction loss to reject this pathology

evaluations.setting: FONDUE-var alternative using early variance-coordinate classification
evaluations.metric: Selected width, variability, and wall time
evaluations.result: Symsol 14-17, dSprites 8.8-9.6, and CelebA 38.6-41.2 depending on one, two, or five epochs
evaluations.baseline: Faster than FONDUE in several settings but rejected because early active/mixed/passive classification is more variable and visually less aligned with the authors' target

limitations: Author-stated: local-neighborhood IDEs can under- or overestimate dimension depending on k, outliers, sample size, and true dimension.
Author-stated: passive coordinates also occur in pathological posterior collapse; the paper discusses reconstruction loss as a distinction but omits it from FONDUE.
Author-stated: the 20% threshold trades compactness against retaining mixed coordinates and may need adjustment.
Author-stated: CelebA reconstruction continues improving after the selected convolutional and fully connected widths.
Reviewer audit: 'optimal' is not defined against a held-out objective or ground-truth best width.
Reviewer audit: only three image datasets, one standard VAE objective, and two old architecture families are tested.
Reviewer audit: the theorem assumes the threshold monotonicity needed by the search and omits a finite failing-width condition.
Reviewer audit: threshold notation in the PDF is off by 100× relative to the intended contemporaneous configuration.
Reviewer audit: the described Levina-Bickel estimator differs from the MacKay-style estimator executed by the code.
Reviewer audit: deterministic-AE applicability is transfer by analogy, because FONDUE cannot operate without mean and sampled posterior representations.
Reviewer audit: the public CelebA score grid has unequal seed coverage at widths 18, 42, 52, and 62.
Reviewer audit: neither carbon emissions nor energy are measured despite being a central motivation.
Reviewer audit: there is no release/tag, pinned environment, test suite, raw search trace, or public selected-model checkpoint for exact reproduction.
Reviewer audit: current direct competitors perform one-training-run relevance learning or ordered bottleneck selection and validate sample quality or known intrinsic dimension more directly.
failure_modes: Global or transient posterior collapse can produce the same large IDE gap as benign excess capacity and cause premature stopping.
A nonmonotone noisy gap can make doubling skip a later passing region or make binary search return the wrong boundary.
If no width crosses the threshold, the unbounded doubling loop does not terminate.
Literal use of t=0.2 with division by 100 applies a 0.2% threshold and changes the selected width dramatically.
Using current repository defaults as if they were the paper code applies an absolute threshold rather than a percentage threshold.
Changing MLE local/global averaging or k−1/k−2 normalization changes the data pivot and every search decision near threshold.
The MLE object's ignored seed and unseeded model initialization prevent exact seed-based replication of Table 1.
High-dimensional distance concentration, duplicate activations, or too few unique samples can destabilize nearest-neighbor IDE.
An underestimated input IDE increases the number of doubling steps; an overestimated one may begin beyond the first crossing and rely on a fabricated zero/one lower bound.
Architecture, likelihood, beta, decoder strength, or optimization changes can move passive-coordinate onset without changing the dataset.
Selecting no passive variables may discard mixed coordinates that improve reconstruction or downstream performance.
Unequal seed coverage can make plotted cross-width trends appear smoother or more certain than the underlying archive supports.
A deterministic autoencoder has no posterior sampling gap, so direct invocation of FONDUE is undefined.
reusable_insights: A discrepancy between stochastic posterior samples and posterior means is a cheap diagnostic for prior-like unused VAE coordinates.
Separate capacity selection from intrinsic-dimension estimation: an architecture's useful bottleneck width need not equal a dataset's manifold dimension or factor count.
Treat posterior collapse as a competing explanation whenever passive-coordinate diagnostics are used for model selection.
Combine the IDE gap with reconstruction, KL, active-coordinate, and held-out quality gates before calling a threshold crossing acceptable.
Any doubling/binary selector needs an explicit maximum width, a monotonicity audit, repeated estimates, and a policy for contradictory evaluations.
Write percentage parameters unambiguously as either 0.2 fractions or 20 percentages, never a mixture of both conventions.
Pin the exact estimator formula, including averaging order and finite-sample correction; the label 'MLE' is insufficient provenance.
Publish raw run-level search traces in addition to aggregated representation scores so selection results can be independently recomputed.
Audit balanced replication at every hyperparameter value before drawing connected curves or uncertainty bands.
Ordered or relevance-learning bottlenecks can amortize width selection into one training run and provide a stronger modern baseline than repeated short-run binary search.
For transfer from VAE to AE, validate the selected width on the target objective rather than assuming stochastic and deterministic bottlenecks share an optimum.
open_questions: Does the early mean-sample IDE boundary predict the held-out likelihood, FID, rate-distortion curve, or downstream utility of a fully retrained VAE?
How sensitive are selected widths to threshold, MLE formula, k, sample count, metric, posterior draw, and integer rounding?
How often is the pass/fail sequence actually nonmonotone across seeds and modern VAE families?
Can a finite-width confidence interval replace the deterministic threshold and trigger additional runs only near ambiguity?
What reconstruction/KL gate reliably separates benign polarization from posterior collapse after one epoch?
Would one-run ARD, ordered bottlenecks, neuron pruning, or projected-loss estimators dominate FONDUE at equal compute?
Does the method remain useful for hierarchical, discrete, hyperspherical, vector-quantized, diffusion, and text VAEs?
Can the raw 2022 FONDUE runs and selected checkpoints be recovered and linked with exact configs and seeds?
Which CelebA models are missing from the score archive, and were the published plots recomputed with unequal seed counts?
Can the theorem be replaced by a stochastic bracketing guarantee with a finite cap and noisy monotonicity violations?
Is a VAE-selected width ever reliably optimal for a deterministic AE under changes in decoder capacity or training objective?

competitive_landscape.title: Adaptive Compression of the Latent Space in Variational Autoencoders
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct post-publication competitor for automatic VAE bottleneck-width selection with reduced search cost.
competitive_landscape.difference: Sejnova et al. shrink the bottleneck during one training process by neuron removal and compare the resulting model directly with grid-search optima on four image datasets, including performance after selection. FONDUE instead trains multiple short-run models and detects an IDE-gap boundary, which is less invasive but does not validate the final chosen model against an explicit optimum.

competitive_landscape.title: ARD-VAE: A Statistical Formulation to Find the Relevant Latent Dimensions of Variational Autoencoders
competitive_landscape.relationship: Strongest accepted direct competitor for learning relevant VAE coordinates automatically.
competitive_landscape.difference: ARD-VAE introduces a hierarchical prior that estimates axis relevance within one model and evaluates known-factor recovery, disentanglement, FID, precision, and recall on synthetic and real datasets through ImageNet. It changes the VAE prior and needs a nominal maximum width, whereas FONDUE is an external selector for a standard VAE; nevertheless ARD-VAE supplies the quality validation and modern baselines absent from FONDUE.
competitive_landscape.source_version: WACV 2025 oral, accepted open-access version; arXiv:2501.10901v2

competitive_landscape.title: Ordered Embeddings and Intrinsic Dimensionalities with Information-Ordered Bottlenecks
competitive_landscape.relationship: One-run ordered-bottleneck alternative that directly estimates global intrinsic dimension and supports truncation without retraining.
competitive_landscape.difference: IOB trains nested prefix bottlenecks so early coordinates carry the most likelihood-relevant information, then evaluates reconstruction versus prefix width and estimates intrinsic dimension on high-dimensional synthetic and semantic embeddings. It modifies the architecture and objective but amortizes all candidate widths into one model and works beyond VAEs; FONDUE preserves a standard VAE but retrains at each queried width and equates passive-coordinate onset with optimality.
competitive_landscape.source_version: Machine Learning: Science and Technology 6 (2025) 035010, DOI 10.1088/2632-2153/ade94d; arXiv:2305.11213v1

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding Variational Autoencoders with Intrinsic Dimension and Information Imbalance
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct independent successor testing the paper's claim that VAE representation geometry changes when bottleneck width exceeds data intrinsic dimension.
competitive_landscape.difference: Camboulin et al. combine intrinsic dimension with information imbalance, identify a width-dependent transition and two distinct training phases, and emphasize that late generalization dynamics differ from rapid early fitting. This richer diagnostic supports the relevance of ID while weakening FONDUE's assumption that one-epoch IDE alone is sufficient for final architecture selection.

competitive_landscape.title: Intrinsic Dimension Estimating Autoencoder (IDEA) Using CancelOut Layer and a Projected Loss
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current autoencoder-based competitor for jointly identifying intrinsic dimension and learning a reconstructive projection.
competitive_landscape.difference: IDEA uses reweighted CancelOut layers and a projected reconstruction loss that explicitly tests removal of an additional coordinate during training, then benchmarks known theoretical dimensions and reconstruction. It targets dataset intrinsic dimension with a deterministic autoencoder rather than standard-VAE capacity, but its ground-truth benchmarks and one-model projected-loss criterion address two major gaps in FONDUE's evidence.
competitive_landscape.source_version: Machine Learning with Applications (2026) 100850; arXiv:2509.10011v3, revised 2026-01-21

novelty_assessment.author_claim: A principled and computationally efficient unsupervised algorithm that finds the optimal VAE or AE latent dimensionality by exploiting early divergence between intrinsic-dimension estimates of posterior means and samples, with more than 35,000 released IDE scores and robustness across architectures.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The mean-sample IDE diagnostic is clearly motivated by passive posterior coordinates, the score deposit is unusually useful for a 2022 preprint, and the doubling/binary search reduces the number and duration of trained candidates in the three demonstrations. The paper predates several stronger one-run relevance and ordered-bottleneck methods. However, the binary-search theorem assumes the empirical single-crossing property, the paper does not compare automatic selectors, and it evaluates no objective that defines an optimal width.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The credible novelty is a simple early-training capacity heuristic plus a broad empirical archive, not a proved or validated solution to optimal latent-dimension selection. The central descriptive signal survives audit, but the method is weakened by a collapse confound, threshold and MLE reporting contradictions, unequal archive replication, unpinned code drift, and narrow evaluation. By 2026, Adaptive Compression, ARD-VAE, IOB, and IDEA offer more direct one-run selection or dimension recovery with stronger final-quality or ground-truth evaluation. FONDUE remains reusable as a diagnostic or bracket initializer if its estimator, threshold, collapse guard, stochastic uncertainty, and stopping cap are made explicit.

reviewer_notes: Audit covered all 17 pages of the exact arXiv v1 PDF, every displayed equation, three algorithms, seven tables, thirteen numbered figures, all references, and Appendices A-G. All pages had usable extracted text and were visually inspected at rendered resolution; plot labels, curves, captions, architecture tables, and algorithm typography were cross-checked against the source assets. The exact PDF and cached text hashes matched the pinned index. The sole arXiv source archive had SHA-256 750103f1b066c045cc5f971fdb829346c4e8463735f53250ca891fa81320e033 and contained 53 files: all TeX, style/bibliography material, algorithm source, and 36 PDF/XML figure assets were inspected, including unused annotated/draft assets. The official Kent score deposit was downloaded and its published MD5 64013274c3e416b4d086cc36a7a48583 verified; its ten TSV files contain 53,685 data rows, and row-level dimensions/seeds exposed the CelebA imbalance. The public code repository was inspected at current HEAD f6d6e66b536bcbe635392d3438338949d4dc8730 and at the last pre-submission revision b0ead6b1d6646be781835bc1ca430b8ef2275dc7; source, configuration, history, documentation, dependencies, seeding, tests, tags, and resource links were audited. Static independent checks confirmed the 100× threshold-text discrepancy and the MLE averaging mismatch. A full empirical rerun was not attempted because the repository has no pinned environment or selected-model artifacts and depends on the retired TensorFlow 2.6 stack; the raw scores were independently aggregated instead. Current primary competitors were checked through 2026-08-24 from arXiv, CVF/WACV, Springer/ICANN metadata, and the IOP publication record.
